local_checks.invariant: Untrusted (fork / pull_request) code never runs with deployment authority or protected secrets; deploy identity is bound to push on main only
local_checks.result: Workflow triggers are `push: branches [main]` and `pull_request` (not pull_request_target). Top-level permissions are contents:read, checks:write, pull-requests:write. The `deploy` job is gated `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'`, uses `environment: production`, and is the only place FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT is referenced (passed to FirebaseExtended/action-hosting-deploy). SUPABASE_DB_URL is referenced only in the step-level `env` of the DB-test step guarded by `if: secrets.SUPABASE_DB_URL != ''`; on fork PRs GitHub supplies no repository secrets for the pull_request event, and same-repo PR authors already hold push rights, so no lower-trust writer reaches a secret. No workflow expression (`github.event.*` fields) is interpolated into any `run:` block, so no expression/command injection surface exists.

local_checks.invariant: Build inputs that reach the shipped artifact are bound by a lockfile and resolve deterministically
local_checks.result: Root package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) pins the packages that scripts/build-web.cjs bundles or copies into public/ (@supabase/supabase-js 2.117.2, esbuild 0.28.2, lucide 1.49.0, tailwindcss 3.4.19, playwright 1.64.1); CI uses `npm ci` for root and `functions/`. build-web.cjs reads only from node_modules and writes only under public/ (no network). GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable major tags (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2, FirebaseExtended/action-hosting-deploy@v0) rather than commit SHAs; the only lower-trust writer would be the third-party action maintainers, which the discipline treats as hardening, not a finding.

local_checks.result: .gitleaks.toml extends default rules and allowlists only the publishable-key pattern, the public Firebase project id, and the generated paths public/vendor/*, public/supabase-client.mjs, package-lock.json; sources of those bundles (src/) remain scanned, and scripts/check-frontend.cjs independently fails the build if `sb_secret_*` or `service_role` appears in a shipped client file. .gitignore excludes .env, .env.local, backend/.env, *.db and a key-pair name; `git ls-files` shows no tracked .env/.pem/.key/credentials files and the 2-commit history adds none. local_checks.invariant: The GITHUB_TOKEN persisted by actions/checkout cannot be used by PR-controlled code for a privileged action

local_checks.invariant: Every table in the supabase_realtime publication has RLS enabled with an owner-or-role SELECT policy, so INSERT/UPDATE change events are only delivered to subscribers whose policy matches the new row; client-chosen filters cannot widen access.

Each has `enable row level security` and exactly one SELECT policy binding user_id/farmer_uid/submitted_by_uid to auth.uid() or a role check (core_schema.sql:301-335, harvest_oil.sql:81-84). No table has REPLICA IDENTITY FULL (grep: none), so old records carry only the primary key. Postgres-changes filters are AND-ed with RLS, not a bypass. Invariant holds for INSERT/UPDATE.

local_checks.invariant: Role revocation/downgrade is reflected in Realtime delivery without re-subscription (no stale authorization in long-lived channels).
local_checks.result: Policies call private.has_any_role -> private.current_app_role (core_schema.sql:24-48), a STABLE definer that reads private.user_roles live on every evaluation; admin_set_user_role upserts that table (admin_tools.sql:38-40). Realtime evaluates the SELECT policy per change with the subscription's claims, so a downgraded reviewer stops receiving others' rows on the next change. local_checks.invariant: DELETE change events on published tables must not reach subscribers who could not SELECT the row.
local_checks.result: Source produces DELETE WAL events on exactly one published table: public.role_applications, via `delete from auth.users` in private.delete_my_account (account_deletion.sql:28) cascading through `references auth.users (id) on delete cascade` (core_schema.sql:65). No application code deletes rows in any other published table (harvest_oil.sql:7 and tree_profiles.sql:4 state 'No DELETE anywhere'; grep confirms). The role_applications SELECT policy is owner-or-admin (core_schema.sql:304-305), but Supabase Realtime documents that RLS is not applied to DELETE events (the old record no longer exists; only primary-key columns are delivered to every subscriber with SELECT privilege on the table). authenticated holds SELECT on role_applications (core_schema.sql:282-285). Table grants to anon: trees_public, tree_events_public (core_schema.sql:286), farmer_profiles (tree_profiles.sql:27) under RLS. Covered.

local_checks.invariant: verify_certificate discloses only non-personal facts for an unguessable serial and is not an enumeration oracle
local_checks.result: Serial validated to FSL-YYYY-16hex via opt_text(40)+regex (:62-71); prefix = 64 bits of a sha256 share id, so enumeration is infeasible; distinct 'format'/'unknown' reasons leak nothing beyond the format. Output: tree id/name, share count, total, land flag, status, issuedAt and holder initials derived from the holder's own display_name (:81-83). Tree lookup ignores listed status (:80) but a certificate necessarily belongs to a formerly listed tree. Pre-auth work: `id like v_prefix||'%'` on text PK (:75) is not index-assisted under a non-C collation and to_char(created_at) is unindexed -> one sequential scan of public.shares per anonymous call; bounded by table size (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: public_status (anon) exposes only coarse ok/degraded flags and performs bounded work
local_checks.result: Output is limited to api/jobs/email flags and a timestamp (:148-153); no counts or error texts. Work: two queries over cron.job_run_details joined to cron.job (:139-147) with no time window; the repo never prunes cron.job_run_details (prune_monitoring deletes only client_errors/email_outbox, monitoring_retention.sql:10-11) while faseela-send-emails runs every minute (~1.4k rows/day). Per-call cost therefore grows without bound and is reachable unauthenticated; actual table size, pg_cron indexes and platform statement_timeout are deployment facts -> hardening with an owner check, not a candidate (no concrete shared impact established).

local_checks.invariant: report_client_error (anon) cannot inject or leak through the admin diagnostics reader (admin_system_status)
local_checks.result: Untyped jsonb fields are coerced with ->> and truncated with left() (:126-140); no dynamic SQL. Attacker-controlled `message` reaches admins via admin_system_status.clientErrors.top (:177-180) and is rendered with escapeHtml in both text and title attribute (public/app.js:17382). user_id is auth.uid() (null for anon). Covered; the anonymous-shared 500/h cap is noted as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: public_tree_profile (anon) returns no uids, no storage paths and only consented/published/listed data
local_checks.result: treeId via req_id regex (:137); farmer block requires consent_public and active assignment and omits farmer_uid and photo_path (hasPhoto boolean only) (:147-153); events limited to status='published' and 30 rows (:159-160); no media paths. The tree row itself is read without the RLS predicate status='listed' (:143) — shared root cause with the SECURITY DEFINER unit, linked here because this is the anon entry surface.

hardening_notes: request_oil (supabase/migrations/20261101000100_harvest_oil.sql:236-241): the open-request count is read before pg_advisory_xact_lock is taken; move the count after the lock so concurrent calls cannot exceed the 3-open-requests cap (bounded by distinct available allocations).

report_client_error (supabase/migrations/20261026000200_notifications_monitoring.sql:134-136): the 500/h cap is one anonymous-shared bucket; 500 trivially cheap unauthenticated calls per hour silently suppress all genuine error reports for the hour and >=50/h triggers an admin ops_alert (once per 6 h). Consider a separate (larger) budget for authenticated callers and/or dropping anon reports first, plus logging the drop count.

public_status (supabase/migrations/20261026000400_profile_onboarding_status.sql:139-147) and admin_system_status (:187-190 of notifications_monitoring.sql) scan cron.job_run_details without a time window, and the repository never prunes that table while faseela-send-emails adds ~1,440 rows/day. Add `delete from cron.job_run_details where end_time < now() - interval '7 days'` to private.prune_monitoring and restrict the status queries to `start_time > now() - interval '1 day'`; owner should check the current row count and whether the anon role's statement_timeout bounds the cost.

verify_certificate (supabase/migrations/20261101000200_certificates.sql:74-76): `id like v_prefix || '%'` on a text PK is not index-assisted under a non-C collation; add an index on public.shares (id text_pattern_ops) or store the serial prefix in an indexed column so the anonymous lookup is O(log n).

farmer_has_tree / operator_has_mill (supabase/migrations/20261026000100_admin_tools.sql:147-148): EXECUTE is granted to authenticated although every caller is SECURITY DEFINER and no public wrapper exists; revoke the grant so a future exposure of schema `private` cannot turn them into assignment oracles for caller-chosen uids.
private.client_errors worst-case footprint is bounded (500/h x 14 days x ~2.6 KB ≈ 0.45 GB) but sizeable for a monitoring table; consider a lower global cap or shorter retention for anon-origin rows.

tree-media Edge Function (supabase/functions/tree-media/index.ts:44 vs :47): event media is filtered to jpg/png/webp before signing but farmerPhoto is not; apply the same extension filter (owned by the Edge unit).
